title: Auto China 2026 Closes with Record 1.28 Million Visitors and 181 World-Debut Vehicles — Largest Auto Show in History Confirms China's Intelligent Mobility Leadership
detail: Auto China 2026 (Beijing International Automotive Exhibition) closed on May 4 with 1.28 million total visitors — making it the largest automobile exhibition in history by attendance. CarNewsChina and CnEVPost reported the final figures: 181 world-debut vehicles (including 71 concept cars) across exhibitors from 15 countries, with Chinese OEMs collectively representing the most dominant domestic showing in the event's history. The 10-day exhibition (April 24–May 4) functioned as a global showcase of China's transition from mass-volume EV manufacturer to intelligent mobility ecosystem leader. CnEVPost's post-show analysis highlighted three dominant themes: (1) LiDAR is now standard equipment on mid-to-high-end Chinese EVs, signaling that full-stack autonomous driving has become a mainstream product feature rather than a premium option; (2) AI-native vehicle cockpits with voice, gesture, and multimodal LLM interaction are replacing traditional infotainment systems across the price spectrum; (3) Chinese brands are making credible plays for European market share with globally certified products meeting Euro NCAP safety standards. The record attendance — up from approximately 900,000 at the 2024 edition — reflects both surging domestic consumer interest in China's new intelligent vehicle generation and significant international auto industry attention. Western auto executives including multiple CEO-level attendees were observed photographing Chinese competitors' vehicles extensively — a dramatic reversal from the 2015 era when Chinese automakers emulated Western designs. The show featured China's first major public demonstration of flying car commercialization: Xpeng's Aridge flying car (7,000 pre-orders by April 27) and EHang autonomous air vehicles drew the largest crowds on the show floor, signaling that urban air mobility is a near-term commercial sector rather than speculative technology in China's industrial roadmap.
